| # Environmental Data {#environmental-data-1 .p_Heading1 style="page-break-after: avoid;"}                                                                                                                                |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

Environmental conditions could be any values of the application software which are stored in the error memory at the occurrence of a fault.\
The values must be provided as \"Signals\".\
The required Environmental Data can be recorded through Signals via ED_Class (Environmental Data Class) mechanism.

## Environmental Data Class (ED_Class): {#environmental-data-class-ed_class .p_Heading2 style="page-break-after: avoid;"}

Environmental Data Classes are eC configurable. The user can configure a maximum of 5 ED Classes.\
Note: The maximum number of bytes of ED Signals allowed per ED_Class is 10. Please ensure that ED Signal size doesn't exceed this limit.

 \
User can configure a maximum of 25 ED Signals.\
Additionally, each ASW DFC is configured with an ED_Class also. So this means, DFCs which are configured to respective ED_Class have their DFES entry mapped with ED Signals of that particular ED_Class.\
So depending on the kind of Signal the values can occupy 2 or 4 bytes of storage (as supported data types for Environment Data Signals in EasyConfig are UINT16, SINT16, UINT32 and SINT32).\
Therefore the number of environmental data depends on the selected (calibrated) Signals configured in EasyConfig.\
The storage is visible as byte array on the calibration tool under the measurement point variable DFES_EnvBlock.\
Note: To read the DTC information stored in NVM, use the UDS service 0x19.

Note: It is possible to replace customer-specific data for Environment data operating hours by using  bds_sys_regOverwriteOpHrsCbk().
